purpose: Verify service guarantees and their tradeoffs, not tune the repeatedly inspected 2025 test period.
method_selection: Retain the validation-selected model and frozen 0.7 carbon / 0.2 peak settings. No new model, weight or deadline tuning. Three-hour readiness is an operator service declaration, not an optimized parameter.
validation: All complete July-August 2025 days, seasonal forecast as available then; default protected site only. Checks implementation, does not select a test-winning policy.
historical_regression: All 122 September-December 2025 days. Previously inspected period; explicitly exploratory.
new_scenario_holdout: Four fixed new site configurations across all 122 days; unseen scenario generalization only, not an unseen historical time window or measured multi-site validation. These specifications are recorded before executing their outcomes.
stress: actual carbon timing reversed with unchanged forecast
unannounced departure two hours after arrival (outside three-hour promise)
at 08:00 add 6kWh to fleet-a with original protected deadline, lock prefix
two-hour deadline is physically impossible for fleet-a
reporting: All attempted rows including infeasible and unserved. Emissions, illustrative cost, peak, delivered/required/unserved, validity and wall time. Savings only on matched fully served pairs. Paired seven-day block intervals for historical forecast ablations are exploratory.
source_policy: Existing separately pinned NESO CI and Open-Meteo ERA5 snapshots, licenses and transformations unchanged. Forecast at midnight sees past CI only. Actual data enters outcome scoring only, never fallback selection.
limits: No physical devices, unannounced load envelope changes, hardware outage, cross-day battery carryover, causal marginal emissions or external commitment timing proof. No model is retrained on test data. New synthetic sites do not validate real-world adoption.
